item.research_question: How do the phonon dynamics of the high-entropy alloy FeCoCrMnNi compare to those of glasses and complex metallic alloys (CMAs), and does it represent a unique class of materials?
item.material_system: Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 (FeCoCrMnNi), a 5-element equiatomic FCC random solid solution
item.processing_route: Polycrystalline samples produced by alloying high-purity elements in an inductively coupled high-frequency levitation furnace, slip-cast into a water-cooled copper mold, and annealed at 1200 °C for 48 h; single crystals grown via the Bridgman technique at 1340 °C with a solidification velocity of 50 mm/h under 200 mbar argon
item.test_conditions: Measurements performed at temperatures of 3, 15, 100, 200, and 300 K using inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS); energy ranges up to 30 meV and wavevectors covering the Brillouin zone
key_findings: Acoustic phonons propagate as well-defined modes throughout the entire Brillouin zone up to energies of 20–30 meV.
Phonon linewidths (ΓFWHM) are significantly broader than in simple monatomic elements but similar to binary alloys of the same constituents.
The observed phonon broadening is primarily attributed to force-constant fluctuations estimated at ~20%, while mass fluctuations contribute negligibly (<0.2 meV).
Phonon attenuation exhibits anisotropy, with longitudinal modes showing multiple regimes and transverse modes showing a smoother monotonic increase.
A strong scattering regime following ΓFWHM ∝ (ℏω)4.5±1 is observed up to ~18 meV in the [ζ00] direction, transitioning to (ℏω)1.7±0.2 above this energy.
The Ioffe-Regel limit (where mean free path equals wavelength) occurs only at energies above ~30 meV, much higher than in typical glasses.

The Generalized Vibrational Density of States (GVDOS) shows a linear dependence up to ~12 meV at low temperatures due to magnetic scattering, reverting to Debye-like (ℏω)2 behavior at room temperature.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that the strong phonon attenuation is driven by force-constant fluctuations resulting from the random atomic environment, which are enhanced by the specific chemical disorder of the alloy. This mechanism is distinct from glasses where topological disorder is also present, and from CMAs where the acoustic phase space is reduced by optic modes. The authors note that the force-constant fluctuations per atomic pair (20–50%) are comparable to those in binary alloys, suggesting that increasing the number of elements from 2 to 5 does not necessarily increase phonon attenuation as predicted by some theories.
item.limitations: The study notes that the strong incoherent neutron scattering entangled with the acoustic phonon in neutron data made the fitting procedure challenging for extracting linewidths, necessitating reliance on IXS data. Additionally, the theoretical models used could not reliably reproduce the low-q part of the spectrum due to the small supercell size used in simulations.
item.future_work: The authors propose that larger force-constant fluctuations should be sought by choosing elements with more different characteristics to effectively impact phonon engineering, noting that current HCP and BCC HEAs introduce stronger mass and atomic size disorder that prevents force-constant disorder from dominating.
quotes: HEAs present unique phonon dynamics at the frontier between fully disordered and ordered materials, characterized by long-propagating acoustic phonons in the whole Brillouin zone.

The situation in our HEA is clearly different: first, the continuum of dispersionless excitations is not observed, and second, the acoustic regime extends to much higher energies and wavevectors, up to 22 and 30 meV for TA and LA respectively, close to the Brillouin zone boundary.

Surprisingly, our work seems to suggest that the high entropy mixing of many elements is ineffective in terms of phonon engineering, while it can be used to effectively impact electron transport and thus the electronic contribution to thermal transport.
